mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 8% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when UNRATE exceeds 8% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings for S&P 500 constituents and results in negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of three consecutive months of INDPRO declines exceeding 1%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a broad-based weakening in demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is below 1% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is rising at an annualized rate above 3%, the combination signals accommodative monetary policy with rising inflation, which historically has been associated with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during periods when FEDFUNDS < 1% and CPIAUCSL YoY > 3%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 100,000 coinciding with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 6% signals a tight labor market, which boosts wage pressures and corporate costs, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as markets anticipate higher earnings growth.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when PAYEMS > 100,000 and UNRATE < 6% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation exists between the monthly change in real personal savings (RSAFS) and S&P 500 5-day forward returns: increased household savings during periods of rising equity prices reflects greater wealth effect and risk appetite.
failure_condition: The correlation between monthly RSAFS change and S&P 500 5-day forward returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05) in out-of-sample walk-forward tests.
